verdict: Coinbase closed 2023 with its most profitable quarter of the year — $273M of net income — as the crypto rally lifted transaction revenue 83% from Q3, and a $121M tax-allowance release flattered the bottom line.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted — vs a $2.46 loss a year ago

kpis.label: $USD resources
kpis.note: cash, USDC and investments at year end

segments.name: Transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees from crypto trading — consumer $493M, institutional $37M. Revenue jumped 83% from Q3 as crypto prices and volatility rose into year-end.

segments.name: Subscription and services
segments.note: Steadier income: stablecoin revenue $172M, blockchain rewards $95M, interest income $43M, custodial fees $20M and other services $46M.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Interest earned on Coinbase's own corporate cash.

opex.name: Technology & development
opex.note: Building the platform — engineering and product, including $100M of stock-based pay.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — legal, compliance and the back office. Includes a $15M legal settlement and higher year-end bonus accruals.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising — including seasonal NBA sponsorship — USDC rewards and winning customers. Up 36% from Q3.

opex.name: Other operating expense, net

follow100Note: Of every $100 Coinbase took in, the tax line added $14.74 back — mostly a one-time release of the tax valuation allowance — which is a big part of why $28.67 was kept as profit. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Trading roared back
takeaways.text: Transaction revenue jumped 83% from the third quarter to $529M as crypto prices and volatility climbed into year-end. Consumer trading supplied $493M of it; institutions $37M.

takeaways.title: The steadier business kept growing
takeaways.text: Subscription and services revenue reached $375M — 39% of the total — led by $172M of stablecoin revenue and $95M of blockchain rewards. It is the cushion that keeps Coinbase profitable when trading cools.

takeaways.title: A tax benefit padded the profit
takeaways.text: The tax line was a $141M benefit, $121M of it a non-cash release of the valuation allowance Coinbase had held against its deferred tax assets. That is why net income of $273M is more than double the $133M pre-tax profit.

oneTimers: A $121M non-cash income-tax benefit from releasing part of Coinbase's valuation allowance against its deferred tax assets — the main reason the quarter's $141M tax benefit is so large.
An $18M gain on buying back Coinbase's own debt below face value, inside other income.
$15M of legal settlement costs inside general & administrative expense.
otherDetail: A $52M net gain on crypto Coinbase holds for operations — price recoveries on coins previously written down, net of new impairments — is shown in this step rather than inside operating expenses, alongside $36M of other income (including an $18M gain on repurchasing its own debt) less $19M of interest expense: a net +$69M.
footerNote: Coinbase reports no gross-profit line; 'Transaction expense' — the direct cost of processing trades — is shown as cost of revenue. Coinbase also reports a $52M net crypto-asset impairment gain inside operating expenses; the chart shows that gain in the other-income step instead, so chart operating profit is $64M rather than the reported $116M — net income is unchanged at $273M. Figures are from Coinbase's Q4 2023 shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-K.
